title: Autopsy results for man who died in NRP custody will not be revealed
article: The Special Investigations Unit will not be releasing the results of a preliminary post-mortem for Andrew Campbell, who died in a police holding cell, saying the cause of death lies at the heart of the investigation.
Campbell, a 21-year-old from Nova Scotia, died after being arrested for robbery and assault following an incident Thanksgiving Monday at Lucky's Video on Pine Street North in Thorold.
SIU spokesperson Rose Bliss said that in general the preliminary results would be released only if investigators determine their work will not be jeopardized.

"However, in this particular case, Mr. Campbell's cause and manner of death is pertinent to what we are investigating, so even just talking about preliminary autopsy results could very well jeopardize the integrity of what we are doing," she said.
As well, she said, there are further scientific tests being conducted into the man's death, including toxicology.
"We have to allow those tests to be done and completed and get those results back from that before we can speak conclusively about PM results," Bliss said.

Meanwhile, more information is coming about the Thanksgiving incident itself. Speaking on condition on anonymity, one of the store owners explained that at around 1 p.m. her husband, who was serving a customer at the time, noticed Campbell had put an ice cream bar and candy into his pocket without paying.
Her husband tried to tell Campbell to pay for the goods but was ignored and Campbell, who was with an acquaintance the owners recognize as a regular, left the store.
The owner followed and was punched in the head repeatedly when he tried to confront Campbell outside. She said Campbell threw the candy at her husband, who fell to the ground and was kicked.

The other customer used the store phone to call police and waited for them to arrive to give a statement. She said it was the customers description of Campbell's acquaintance that led to the arrest at a Thorold home.
Her husband went to St. Catharines General Hospital where he was treated for his injuries and released later that day.
Police did not arrest Campbell's companion.
